newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda coffee prices rise for third straight week.
newsitem.headline: Uganda coffee prices rise for third straight week.

text.p: Local prices for Ugandan coffee have risen for the third week running and officials predict a firm and buoyant market until at least the end of July.
Both Kiboko and Fair Average Quality (FAQ coffee) prices rose in the trading week ending May 23, while arabica remained steady at 2,500 to 2,800 shillings per kilo.

An official of the state-run Uganda Coffee Development Authority said local prices would remain "firm and buoyant" in line with the international market with the potential to move up through the Brazilian winter season.
Kiboko rose to 750-800 shillings from 700-750. At the end of April, Kiboko was selling at 600-700 shillings.
FAQ coffee ended at 1,600 to 1,700 shillings, up from the previous week's 1,480 to 1,540. FAQ was 1,350 to 1,450 at the end of April.

Total coffee registrations for the week ending May 23 amounted to 49,754 60-kg bags with Robusta Screen 15 (standard) accounting for 29,344 bags. Screen 12 accounted for 12,560 bags and screen 18 6,650.
Bugisu Arabica registered 1,200 bags -- almost doubling the previous week's 700.
The highest and lowest prices recorded for Robusta screen 15 was 83.20 and 63.00 cents per pound respectively.
